newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico tortilla prices seen higher in '97 - Finamex.
newsitem.headline: Mexico tortilla prices seen higher in '97 - Finamex.

text.p: Mexican brokerage Valores Finamex said Wednesday the government could raise the prices of corn-pancake tortillas twice before the end of 1997.

"The current price of a kilo of tortillas in Mexico is $1.40 peso. We think it possible that the government will raise the price to 1.70 pesos, a 21 percent hike. Toward the end of 1997, it might be raised again to near 2.00 pesos," Finamex analyst Francisco Rivero said in a report.
"Tortilla makers in Mexico have said if price controls in the industry were lifted, the price of a kilo of tortillas would now be between 2.70 and 3.00 pesos," he added.
Agriculture Minister Francisco Labastida Ochoa told Reuters in an interview Tuesday the government was considering hiking tortilla prices. But he stressed that no decision had yet been made.
Labastida said subsidies for the tortilla industry would fall more than 2 billion pesos in 1997 to 4.5 billion pesos from the federal handouts to manufacturers made this year.

"The decrease in the total subsidy in 1997 may be due to several reasons; the possible increase in the controlled price of tortillas, the lesser need for corn imports...and the recent decline in the price of corn," Rivero said.
